Rashi on Nazir 40b:2:1.english: This tanna initially said: To derive [the case of] a nazirite from a metzora is impossible, as one does not derive, etc. - Evidently, the matter was obvious to him that a metzora is [shaved] with a razor.

Rashi on Nazir 40b:2:2.hebrew: והדר אמר ניליף מדינא - מנזיר ומלוים, בהצד השוה שבהן. ומדינא נמי לא מצי למילף, משום דאית בה פירכא דרבא מברניש: שכן אין קרבנו בדלות; תאמר במצורע שכן קרבנו בדלות — בעולה ויורד — דכתיב ביה: ״ואם דל הוא״:
Rashi on Nazir 40b:2:2.english: And he then said: Let us derive [it] from an inference - From a nazirite and the Levites, through the common denominator between them. And he was also unable to derive [it] from an inference, because it is subject to the refutation of Rava of Barnish: For [neither of] their offerings is brought in poverty; will you say [the same] of a leper, whose offering is brought in poverty — with an adjustable [sliding-scale] offering — as it is written concerning him: “And if he is poor” (Leviticus 14:21)?

Rashi on Nazir 40b:3:1.hebrew: א"ל ההיא - דקתני: ״דללמדו ממצורע אי אפשר״, דמשמע דפשיטא ליה דמצורע הוי בתער — אליבא דרבנן היא, דגמרי לה מ״זקנו״ ו״פאת״ כדמסיק. והאי דקא בעי: ״מדינא לא אפשר?״, משום דאית ביה למפרך כדפריכנא — אליבא דר' אליעזר, דגמיר לה מנזיר דלקמן:
Rashi on Nazir 40b:3:1.english: [Rava] said to him: That [source] - That which was taught, "that it is impossible to derive it from a leper," which implies that it was obvious to him that a leper is [shaved] with a razor, is in accordance with [the view of] the Rabbis, who derive it from "his beard" and "the corner [of their beard]," as [the Gemara] concludes later. And this [discussion], where [the Gemara] asks: "Is [derivation] by logical deduction not possible?" [and concludes that it is not] because it can be refuted as we refuted [it], is in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Eliezer, who derives it from [the case of] a nazirite below.

Rashi on Nazir 40b:3:2.english: As we learned in a mishna - In tractate Makkot.

Rashi on Nazir 40b:3:3.english: And one is not liable - For rounding the head until he removes it with a razor.

Rashi on Nazir 40b:3:4.hebrew: ר' אליעזר אומר - אפי' במלקט וברהיטני:
Rashi on Nazir 40b:3:4.english: Rabbi Eliezer says - Even with tweezers or with a plane [he is liable].

Rashi on Nazir 40b:4:1.hebrew: ואמרינן מ"ט דרבנן - דלא מחייבי בהקפה אלא בתער:
Rashi on Nazir 40b:4:1.english: And we say, “What is the reason of the Rabbis?” - That they do not hold [one] liable for rounding [the head] except with a razor.

Rashi on Nazir 40b:4:2.hebrew: דתניא זקנו - האמור לגבי מצורע, מה ת"ל? והלא "כל שערו" במשמע, וזקנו בכלל שערו! אלא, לפי שנאמר לגבי כהנים: "ופאת זקנם לא יגלחו", יכול אפי' כהן מצורע המתגלח לא יגלח פאת זקנו? ת"ל: וגילח זקנו:
Rashi on Nazir 40b:4:2.english: As it is taught: “His beard” - Which is stated regarding a leper: What does the verse teach? For is not “all his hair” [already] implied, and his beard is included in his hair! Rather, because it is stated regarding priests, “Neither shall they shave off the corners of their beard” (Leviticus 21:5), one might have thought that even a priest who is a leper undergoing shaving may not shave the corner of his beard; [therefore,] the verse states: “and he shall shave... his beard.”

Rashi on Nazir 40b:5:1.hebrew: ומנלן - דהך גילוח בתער קאי? דתניא: ״ופאת זקנם״:
Rashi on Nazir 40b:5:1.english: And from where do we derive - That this shaving refers to [shaving] with a razor? As it is taught: “Neither shall they shave off the corners of their beards.”

Rashi on Nazir 40b:5:2.hebrew: ת"ל - גבי ישראל: ״לא תשחית פאת זקנך״. אי ״לא תשחית״, יכול ליקטו במלקט וברהיטני יהא חייב? ת"ל: ״ופאת זקנם לא יגלחו״. הא כיצד? גילוח שיש בו השחתה דיבר הכתוב, ואיזו? הוי אומר: בתער. מהו גילוח דקאסר ליה רחמנא גבי הקפת הראש והשחתת פאת זקן, ואישתרי ליה גבי מצורע, דמותר הוא בו? היינו תער: מאי משמע לן מהכא דמצורע לא הוי אלא בתער? דלמא לעולם אימא לך דאפי' ליקטו במלקט וברהיטני שפיר דמי, והאי דקתני ״זקנו״ מה ת"ל — דאתא לאשמועי' דאפי' גילחו בתער לא מיחייב עליה משום ״פאת זקנם לא יגלחו״:
Rashi on Nazir 40b:5:2.english: The verse states - Regarding an Israelite, [the verse states]: “Neither shall you destroy the corners of your beard” (Leviticus 19:27). If [the Torah had said only] “Neither shall you destroy,” one might think that if he plucked it with tweezers or with a plane he should be liable; [therefore] the verse states [regarding priests]: “Neither shall they shave off the corners of their beards” (Leviticus 21:5). How so? The verse spoke of a shaving that entails destruction; and which is that? You must say: with a razor. What is the shaving that the Merciful One prohibited regarding rounding the [corners of the] head and destroying the corners of the beard, and was permitted to a leper, in that he is permitted [to shave] with it? That is a razor. What indicates to us from here that a leper [is shaved] only with a razor? Perhaps I could actually tell you that even if he plucked it with tweezers or with a plane, it is well [and fulfills the mitzvah]; and that which [the baraita] teaches, “What does the verse teach [by stating] ‘his beard’?” — it comes to teach us that even if he shaved it with a razor, he is not liable for it on account of “Neither shall they shave off the corners of their beards”.

Rashi on Nazir 40b:8:1.hebrew: אי ס"ד דכי ליקטו במלקט וברהיטני שפיר דמי - ומצוה קעביד — לישתוק קרא מיניה ולא ליכתוב זקנו, ואמינא: ליקטו במלקט וברהיטני שפיר דמי, דמייתינן לה מדינא:
Rashi on Nazir 40b:8:1.english: If it should enter your mind that if he removed it with tweezers or with a plane, it is well - And he performs a mitzva [thereby] — let the verse be silent regarding it and not write "his beard," and I would say: Removing it with tweezers or with a plane is well, for we derive it by logical deduction.

Rashi on Nazir 40b:8:2.english: And just as with regard to a nazirite, who performs a transgression - When he shaves with a razor during the days of [his] naziriteship.

Rashi on Nazir 40b:8:3.hebrew: אפילו הכי מיחייב - כי ליקטן במלקט וברהיטני, כדאמרינן לעיל: לרבות כל המעבירין:
Rashi on Nazir 40b:8:3.english: Even so, he is liable - When he plucked them with tweezers or with a plane, as we said above: “To include all [implements] that remove [hair].”

Rashi on Nazir 40b:8:4.hebrew: הכא - דכי מגלח מצוה קעביד, כדכתיב: "וגילח את כל שערו":
Rashi on Nazir 40b:8:4.english: Here - That when he shaves, he is performing a mitzvah, as it is written: "And he shall shave all his hair."

Rashi on Nazir 40b:8:5.hebrew: לא כל שכן - שבכל דבר מותר לגלח, ואפילו בתער:
Rashi on Nazir 40b:8:5.english: [Is it] not all the more so - That it is permitted to shave with any implement, and even with a razor.

Tosafot on Nazir 40b:1:1.hebrew: אין קרבנו בדלות - אלא קרבן קבוע, בין עניים בין עשירים. תאמר במצורע שאם עני הוא מביא צפורים, וא"כ גם לא נחמיר עליו להטעינו תער! ואין להקשות: לפי מה שמסקינן דיליף מצורע מקרא אחרינא, שלא בנזיר — דהיינו בנזיר דבסמוך — ולייתי נזיר במה הצד? דאיכא למיפרך: שכן אינו בשאלה, או שכן שכל גופו טעון תגלחת:
Tosafot on Nazir 40b:1:1.english: "His offering is not [brought] in poverty" - Rather, [a nazirite and a Levite have] a fixed offering, whether for the poor or for the rich. Will you say [the same] with regard to a leper, for if he is poor he brings birds, and if so, we should also not be stringent with him to require him [to shave with] a razor?! And one should not object: According to that which we conclude, that [the requirement of a razor for] a leper is derived from another verse without [needing the verse regarding] a nazirite — that is, [the verse] regarding a nazirite [cited] nearby — let a nazirite [instead] be derived via the common denominator [of a leper and the Levites]? For [such a derivation] can be refuted: For [they share the feature] that they are not subject to absolution [of a vow], or that their entire body requires shaving.

Tosafot on Nazir 40b:2:1.hebrew: והאי תנא מעיקרא - בברייתא דלעיל קאמר: "ללמדו ממצורע אי אפשר" כו' — אלמא דקים ליה לתנא [תער] במצורע בלא נזיר, שהרי בא נזיר ממצורע. ובהך ברייתא בעי למילף מצורע דבעי תער מדינא דנזיר ולוים — אלמא מצורע גופיה לא יליף אלא מנזיר! ומדינא נמי לא אייתי, [דקאמר]: "מה להצד" כו', וסוף לומדו מ"ראשו" דכתיב בנזיר; ומ"מ רבי אליעזר לא ידע תער במצורע אלא מנזיר, כדמפרש והולך:
Tosafot on Nazir 40b:2:1.english: "And this tanna initially" - In the baraita above (39b), it states: "It is impossible to learn it from a metzora..." etc. — which shows that it is established for the tanna [that a razor is required] for a metzora without [relying on] a nazirite, for the nazirite was to be derived from a metzora. Yet in this baraita (40a), he seeks to derive that a metzora requires a razor from an inference from a nazirite and Levites — which implies that the metzora himself is derived only from a nazirite! And from the inference he did not establish [it] either, [as the Gemara refutes]: "What [is the common denominator] between them..." etc., and ultimately he derives it from "his head," which is written in connection with a nazirite; and nevertheless, Rabbi Eliezer knew [the requirement of] a razor for a metzora only from a nazirite, as [the Gemara] continues to explain.

Tosafot on Nazir 40b:2:2.hebrew: דתנן בפרק בתרא דמכות (דף כ.) אינו חייב כו' - לגבי פיאות דזקן תניא, דאין חייבין בהשחתת פאת זקן, בין כהנים בין ישראלים, עד שיטלנו בתער. ור"א אמר: אפי' ליקטו במלקט ורהיטני מיחייב:
Tosafot on Nazir 40b:2:2.english: "As we learned" in the last chapter of Makkot (20a): "He is not liable, etc." - It is taught regarding the corners of the beard, that they are not liable for destroying the corner of the beard, whether priests or Israelites, unless he removes it with a razor; and Rabbi Eliezer says: Even if he removed it with tweezers or a plane, he is liable.

Tosafot on Nazir 40b:4:1.hebrew: ומאי טעמייהו דרבנן - כלומר: מהיכא נפקא לן דפשיטא להו דמצורע בתער אפילו בלא נזיר, כדס"ל? דתניא: "זקנו" מה ת"ל? במצורע כתיב: "והיה ביום השביעי יגלח את כל שערו את ראשו ואת זקנו" וכו', והלא בכלל "כל שערו" הוא, ולמה פרט "זקנו"? לפי שנא' גבי כהנים: "ופאת זקנם לא יגלחו", יכול אף מצורע — כלומר, כהן והוא מצורע — כן, שלא יכול לגלח זקנו, והא דכתיב "וגלח את כל שערו" ע"כ לבר מזקנו, א"נ בנמרט זקנו, שאין עשה דגילוח דוחה לאו דהשחתת זקן הכהנים ועשה דקדושים דכהנים; ת"ל "זקנו" — מיותר שנכתב במצורע, לאשמועינן: עשה דזקנו דחי לאו ד"לא יגלחו" בכהנים ועשה ד"קדושים יהיו". ואע"פ שאין עשה דוחה לא תעשה ועשה בעלמא, הכא דחי, כדאמר בריש יבמות (דף ה.), דהאי לאו ועשה שאינו שוה [בכל] הוא, דהשחתת זקן אינו בנשים, כדאמר פ"ק דקדושין (דף לה:). וא"ת: ודלמא אתי למישרי לאו גרידא ד"לא תשחית פאת זקנך"? וי"ל (דמשער): דאיכא למימר קרא סתמא כתיב בה, בישראל ככהנים. ועי"ל, והוא העיקר: דע"כ לרבנן ללאו גרידא דישראל לא איצטריך קרא, דנפקא להו מ"ראשו", מקרא קמא, דדחי עשה דמצורע לאו דהקפה, דסבירא להו דהקפת כל הראש שמה הקפה, כדאיתא בסמוך; א"כ, "זקנו" לא איצטריך קרא אלא לכהנים, ולאשמועינן דעשה דמצורע דחי לאו ועשה דהשחתת זקן הכהנים (גרידא). ומדאתא קרא דזקנו למישרי לו לאו דהשחתת זקן, והשחתת זקן לא מחייב אלא בתער — מכלל דמצורע תגלחתו אינו אלא בתער; דאם לא כן, "זקנו" למה לי:
Tosafot on Nazir 40b:4:1.english: "And what is the reason of the Rabbis?" - That is to say: From where do we derive [this, given] that it is obvious to them that a metzora [shaves] with a razor even without [deriving it from] a nazir, as they hold? For it is taught [in a baraita]: "'His beard' — what does the verse teach? Regarding a metzora it is written: 'And it shall be on the seventh day that he shall shave all his hair: his head and his beard...' (Leviticus 14:9), etc. And is [the beard] not included in 'all his hair'? So why did [the verse] specify 'his beard'? Because it is stated regarding priests: 'Neither shall they shave off the corners of their beard' (Leviticus 21:5). One might have thought that even a metzora — that is to say, a priest who is a metzora — should also be so, that he would not be able to shave his beard, and that which is written: 'and he shall shave all his hair' is perforce excluding his beard; or alternatively, [that the verse speaks of a case] where his beard fell out, since the positive commandment of shaving does not override the negative commandment against destroying the beard of the priests and the positive commandment of [priests being] holy (Leviticus 21:6). [Therefore,] the verse states 'his beard' — which is superfluous where it is written regarding a metzora — to teach us that the positive commandment of 'his beard' overrides the negative commandment of 'they shall not shave' regarding priests and the positive commandment of 'they shall be holy.'" And even though generally a positive commandment does not override a negative commandment and a positive commandment [combined], here it overrides [them], as [the Gemara] says at the beginning of Yevamot (5a), that this negative commandment and positive commandment are not equal in everyone (i.e., do not apply to all), since destroying the beard does not apply to women, as [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Kiddushin (35b). And if you should ask: But perhaps it comes to permit merely the plain negative commandment of 'You shall not destroy the corners of your beard' (Leviticus 19:27)? One can answer (as is surmised) that it can be said that the verse is written without qualification, regarding an Israelite just as regarding priests. And another answer can be given, and it is the primary [explanation]: that perforce according to the Rabbis, for a plain negative commandment of an Israelite a verse was not needed, as they derive it from 'his head' in the earlier verse, that the positive commandment of a metzora overrides the negative commandment of rounding [the corners of the head], since they hold that rounding the entire head is considered rounding, as is stated nearby [41a]. If so, the verse 'his beard' was needed only for priests, to teach us that the positive commandment of a metzora overrides the negative commandment and positive commandment of destroying the beard of the priests (alone). And since the verse 'his beard' came to permit to him the negative commandment of destroying the beard, and one is liable for destroying the beard only with a razor, by implication, a metzora's shaving is only with a razor; for if that were not so, why do I need 'his beard'?

Tosafot on Nazir 40b:5:1.hebrew: דבתער - כלומר: חיוב השחתת זקן מנא להו לרבנן דלא הוי אלא בתער, דמינה ילפינן תער למצורע:
Tosafot on Nazir 40b:5:1.english: That [it is] with a razor - That is to say: From where do the Rabbis derive that liability for destroying the beard is only with a razor, from which we derive [the requirement of] a razor for a leper?

Tosafot on Nazir 40b:5:2.hebrew: דתניא ופאת זקנם לא יגלחו - בכהנים כתיב. "יכול אפי' במספרים יהא חייב? ת"ל: 'ולא תשחית פאת זקנך' " — בישראל כתיב. ובמספרים ליכא השחתה, שאינו נוטל השער מעיקרו ושרשו:
Tosafot on Nazir 40b:5:2.english: As it is taught: “Neither shall they shave off the corners of their beards” - [This] is written with regard to priests. “One might [think] he should be liable even [if he shaved] with scissors? The verse states: ‘Neither shall you destroy the corner of your beard’ ” — [which] is written with regard to Israelites. And with scissors there is no destruction, for it does not remove the hair from its base and root.

Tosafot on Nazir 40b:5:3.hebrew: אי לא תשחית יכול אפי' במלקט ורהיטני יהא חייב - שאף הם משחיתים השער מעיקרו, ת"ל: "ופאת זקנם לא יגלחו" — והם אינם קרויים גילוח, שאינם רגילים לגלח בהם:
Tosafot on Nazir 40b:5:3.english: “If ‘Neither shall you destroy,’ one might think [that] even with tweezers and a plane he should be liable” - For they too destroy the hair from its root; [therefore,] the verse states: “Neither shall they shave off the corners of their beards,” and these are not called “shaving,” as people are not accustomed to shave with them.

Tosafot on Nazir 40b:6:1.hebrew: הא כיצד גילוח שיש בו השחתה הוי אומר זה תער - והאי שרא רחמנא במצורע. אי נמי, בקידושין גמרינן פאה פאה כהנים מישראלים. ופריך: ממאי דתגלחת מצורע ליכא אלא בתער? דילמא אפי' במלקט ורהיטני קיים המצורע מצות גילוח, וקרא דזקנו אתא לאשמועינן דאם בא לגלח [בתער] הרשות בידו — שהוא [מוזהר] עליו בעלמא בפאה דזקן, הכא שרי ולא מיחייב. ומשני: אמרי, כלומר [על כרחך] זקנו דכתיב — שזקוק לגלח ולעשות בתער ולא בדבר אחר; דאי ס"ד כי עביד נמי במלקט ורהיטני שפיר דמי, לשתוק קרא מיניה, דאם בא [למימר] שהרשות בידו לגלח בתער פאת זקנו — להא לא בעי קרא דזקנו, דרשות ידעינן מק"ו:
Tosafot on Nazir 40b:6:1.english: “How so? What is shaving that involves destruction? You must say this is a razor” - And this [shaving with a razor] the Merciful One permitted for a leper. Alternatively, in Kiddushin (35b) we derive [via the verbal analogy of] “corner” [and] “corner” [the laws of] priests from Israelites. And [the Gemara] asks: From where [do we know] that the shaving of a leper can only be [performed] with a razor? Perhaps even [if he removed it] with tweezers or a plane, the leper fulfills the mitzvah of shaving, and the verse stating “his beard” comes to teach us that if he wishes to shave [with a razor], he has permission to do so — for [while] in general he is [prohibited] from doing so regarding the corner of the beard, here it is permitted and he is not liable. And [the Gemara] answers: “They say,” that is to say, [perforce] when “his beard” is written, [it means] that he is required to shave and perform [the mitzvah] with a razor and not with anything else; for if it should enter your mind that if he does [so] with tweezers or a plane too it is acceptable, let the verse be silent regarding it, for if it comes [to say] that he has permission to shave the corner of his beard with a razor, for this [the Torah] does not need the verse of “his beard,” as permission we would [already] know from an a fortiori argument.

Tosafot on Nazir 40b:8:1.hebrew: ה"ג ומה נזיר כו' - הוה מצי למפרך: דכהן מצורע לא אתי, שכן ריבה הכתוב [בהן] מצות יתירות — וכה"ג פריך בכל דוכתי — ולכך לא לידחי עשה דמצורע לאו דכהנים. ועוד: מה לנזיר — שכן לאו גרידא, דדחי לאו דהקפה; תאמר בכהנים, דאיכא לאו ועשה: לאו דהשחתת זקן ועשה?! לכ"נ, דעיקר אפירכא אחרונה סמיך, דפריך מרשב"ל:
Tosafot on Nazir 40b:8:1.english: This is the text reading: "And just as a nazirite, etc." - [The Gemara] could have refuted [this]: that a priest who is a leper cannot be derived [from a nazirite], for Scripture multiplied additional commandments for them [priests] — and [the Gemara] raises such a refutation everywhere — and therefore, the positive commandment of a leper should not override the prohibition of priests. And furthermore: what [comparison is there] to a nazirite, in that [there is] a mere negative commandment, as it overrides the prohibition of rounding [the head]; can you say [the same] regarding priests, where there are [both] a negative commandment and a positive commandment: the prohibition against destroying the beard and a positive commandment? Therefore, it appears that [the Gemara] primarily relied on the latter refutation, which it refutes from Reish Lakish.

Tosafot on Nazir 40b:8:2.hebrew: ה"ג ומה נזיר דאיסורא קעביד - ואפילו נזיר טהור חוטא קצת, כדאיתא פ"ק דנדרים (דף י.), ולעיל בפ' שלישי (נזיר דף יט.). ועוד, דמנזיר טמא קא יליף, שגם הוא תגלחתו כתוב בתער, כדמשמע בסמוך, דגמרינן טהור מטמא וטמא מטהור; ואפ"ה תגלחת מצוה דידיה דחי לאו דהקפה, דסבירא ליה דהקפת כל הראש שמה הקפה. ולעולם "מיחייב" — פי': מיחייב לגלח כל ראשו ולדחות לאו דהקפת הראש; מצורע דמצוה — לא כל שכן:
Tosafot on Nazir 40b:8:2.english: This is the reading: "And just as with regard to a nazirite, who performs a transgression" - For even a ritually pure nazirite is considered somewhat of a sinner, as is stated in the first chapter of Nedarim (10a) and above in the third chapter (Nazir 19a). And furthermore, [the Gemara] is deriving [this] from an impure nazirite, regarding whom it is also written that his shaving is with a razor, as is implied nearby [41a], where we derive a pure [nazirite] from an impure [nazirite] and an impure from a pure. And even so, his mitzvah shaving overrides the negative commandment of rounding [the head], as he holds that rounding the entire head is considered rounding. And indeed, [the term] "is obligated" [michayav] means: he is obligated to shave his entire head and override the negative commandment of rounding [the head]; [if so, regarding] a leper, where [his shaving] is a mitzvah, does it not follow all the more so?

Tosafot on Nazir 40b:8:3.hebrew: דמצוה - מצות המקרא תגלחת, ולא באה לו ע"י שום איסור; לכ"ש שתגלחתו דמצוה תדחה לאו דהשחתה! ואי קשה: מה לנזיר שכן קרבנו טעון לחם, כדפ"ל? וי"ל: דלא דמי; דודאי לעיל, דבעינן להטעין תער למצורע ולא שאר משחיתים, פריך שפיר דמ"ה בנזיר דין הוא שיהא טעון תער לתגלחתו, שכמו כן חומרא אחרת בו — שקרבנו טעון לחם. אבל הכא, דלא בעינן למילף להטעין תער במצורע מתגלחת דנזיר, רק שהרשות יהיה בידו להעבירו בתער כמו בשאר משחיתין — ולא שייכא כלל ההיא פירכא, דלא בעינן למילף חומרא מנזיר. אלא מכל מקום תימה הוא: והא הך סוגיא לרבנן, [והרי] מוכח דלרבנן פשיטא להו תער מתגלחת דמצורע מקמי דידעינן ליה בנזיר, דקאמר בברייתא דלעיל: "ללמדו ממצורע אי אפשר" כו', אלמא במצורע פשיטא להו לרבנן דטעון תער לתגלחתו (נזיר); והכא, אי לאו ק"ו דמנזיר, לא אתי [להו] תער במצורע? וי"ל: דאפילו לא קים לו דמצות נזיר בתער, מ"מ שפיר ילפינן ק"ו מנזיר: דדחי תגלחת דידיה פיאות דהקפת הראש, דאיכא בהו לאו במקיף במספרים, כדמשמע בסמוך — מצורע לא כל שכן שיהא מותר לגלח אף בתער, וידחה לאו דהשחתת זקן? אלא ע"כ קרא דזקנו אתא להטעינו תער ולא משחיתים אחרים:
Tosafot on Nazir 40b:8:3.english: Where [his shaving is] a mitzva - The commandment of the biblical text is shaving, and it did not come about for him through any transgression; all the more so should his shaving, which is a mitzva, override the negative commandment against destroying [the corners of the beard]! And if [one should] raise a difficulty: What [is unique] about a nazirite? That his offering requires loaves [of bread], as explained above [40a]! And one can say: It is not comparable. For certainly above, where we sought to require a razor for a metzora and not other hair-destroying [implements], it rightly challenged that for this reason, in the case of a nazirite, it is logical that he should require a razor for his shaving, as likewise there is another stringency regarding him — that his offering requires bread. However here, where we do not seek to derive to require a razor for a metzora from the shaving of a nazirite, but merely that he should have permission to remove [the hair] with a razor as with other hair-destroying [implements] — that refutation is not relevant at all, as we do not seek to derive a stringency from a nazirite. Nevertheless, it is astonishing: Isn't this sugya according to the Rabbis? And it is proven that for the Rabbis, [the requirement of] a razor in the shaving of a metzora is obvious to them before we know it with regard to a nazirite, as the baraita above states: "To derive it from a metzora is impossible..." etc., which shows that with regard to a metzora, it was obvious to the Rabbis that he requires a razor for his shaving; yet here, were it not for the a fortiori inference from a nazirite, a razor in the case of a metzora would not be derived for them? And one can say: Even if it were not established for him that the mitzva of a nazirite is with a razor, nevertheless we rightly derive an a fortiori inference from a nazirite: For just as his shaving overrides the corners [of the head] in rounding the head, which involves a negative commandment [even] when rounding with scissors, as is implied nearby — does it not follow all the more so for a metzora that it should be permitted to shave even with a razor, and it should override the negative commandment against destroying the beard? Rather, perforce the verse "his beard" came to require a razor for him, and not other hair-destroying implements.
